answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid where every agent must reach a specific yarrow zone to certify position. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates acting as a walnut anchor, and each receipt proves physical occupancy. A verifier listens for a gale of signal noise to detect relay fraud, triggering a permanent penalty upon any latency drift. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach sites, while 1,000 fake identities incur unsustainable signal congestion and immediate banishment for failing replay verification.
